theater: 洛陽城與洛水北岸（河南洛陽）

battle.name: 洛陽之戰
battle.theater: 洛陽城與洛水北岸（河南洛陽）
battle.brief: 建德四年（564年）秋冬，北周武帝宇文邕再遣大將軍王軌等率師東出，進逼洛陽；陳宣帝遣大將軍賀若弼、韓擒虎等率眾赴洛陽，據城固守。周軍以撞車、雲梯攻城，陳軍以弓弩、長矛居高拒之，攻而不克，糧道屢遭騎兵襲擾，值歲暮天寒，遂引還。此役勝負不在破城，而在攻城技術與糧秣補給之爭；卡面埃及長矛，正是兩軍步卒倚重的刺擊長兵。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 洛陽之戰是北周與南陳在河南洛陽一線的邊境交戰，發生於北周建德四年、南陳太建六年，即公元564年。交戰的一方是北周：都城長安，疆域含關中、巴蜀與河南，東面以洛陽為最重要的一處軍事樞紐，洛州治所即在洛陽城。北周的兵制以府兵為骨幹，兼有募兵與州郡鎮兵，資源來自關中與關東的屯田；對洛陽的守備與對陳的出擊，都仰賴自關中沿黃河、洛水運來的糧秣，以及洛陽城內的倉儲。另一方是南陳：都城建康（今南京），疆域以長江中下游為主，採荊、揚、益三州並立的結構，江陵的荊州與建康的揚州是兩大支柱，益州提供蜀地的人力與物產。陳的北線據點為壽春、合肥一線，前出在淮水南北，與周的洛州、徐州接壤；陳軍水軍之強，是它在長江防線上得以長期抗衡北方的前提，但北伐能力有限，必須靠江陵與淮南之間的水陸聯運把糧秣送到前線。兩國之間維持著形式上的邦交，互有使節往來，邊境亦有榷場互市，然而荊襄與淮南一線的衝突從未真正停過。
countriesEn: The Battle of Luoyang was a frontier engagement between Northern Zhou and the Chen dynasty fought on the Luoyang line in Henan, in Northern Zhou's fourth year of Jiande and the sixth year of Chen's Taijian, that is, in 564 CE. One of the belligerents was Northern Zhou: its capital was Chang'an, its territories covered Guanzhong, Shu and Henan, and on its eastern side the single most important military pivot was Luoyang, where the seat of Luozhou stood. Zhou's military system rested on the fubing as its backbone, supplemented by recruited troops and by the garrison of the commanderies and prefectures, with the resources drawn from the tuntian of Guanzhong and of the lands east of it; both the holding of Luoyang and the strikes against Chen relied on grain brought down from Guanzhong along the Yellow River and the Luo River, and on the granaries inside the city of Luoyang itself. The other side was the Chen dynasty: its capital was Jiankang, in what is now Nanjing, its lands lay chiefly along the middle and lower Yangtze, and it was organised as three parallel circuits of Jing, Yang and Yi, with Jingzhou at Jiangling and Yangzhou at Jiankang as the two pillars and Yizhou supplying men and goods from the lands of Shu. Chen's northern line ran through Shouchun and Hefei, projecting north and south of the Huai in contact with Zhou's Luozhou and Xuzhou; the strength of Chen's river fleet was the precondition on which it held the long line of the Yangtze against the north for so long, but its capacity for striking north was limited, and grain had to be carried up to the front by water and land together out of Jiangling and out of Huainan. Between the two states a formal diplomatic relationship was maintained, envoys passed in both directions, and markets were established along the frontier, yet the fighting on the Jingxiang and Huainan lines never truly ceased.
people: 這場戰役留下姓名者，多為統兵之將，而各家記載對其分工的安排略有出入。北周方面，發動此役的是周武帝宇文邕。他自560年即位，先以誅除宗室的手法削去宇文氏內部的枝蔓，再整頓府兵、鼓勵屯田，於是把北周推到可與北齊相持的位置；他要的是打通洛陽往荊州的通道，把陳的北線擠回長江以南。史冊記載北方統兵者為大將軍王軌，此人在其後十年間兩度大破陳軍，是周在河南經略的主要將領之一。隨國公楊堅時任丞相，此役中在軍中參贊，《隋書·高祖紀》記其從征伐陳而見用於軍中，其後在北周宗室之間的權力傾軋中步步高升，最終在隋文帝時登基。陳方的主帥是宣帝陳頊，559年即位，經大建年間的整頓，陳的財政與軍力都回穩，得以頂住北周接連數年的北伐。陳將之中可與此役掛鈎者，史料常提賀若弼、韓擒虎、吳明徹、歐陽頠與袁君正：賀若弼與韓擒虎是陳的宿將，後來都成了隋滅陳時的名將；吳明徹是陳在水陸兩用戰術上最倚重的大將；歐陽頠鎮守荊州，掩護洛陽戰場的西翼；袁君正以司州刺史之任，與前線的守城直接相關。真正左右洛陽命運的，其實是陳將司馬消難的出降：他在數年之後投向北周，供出陳軍的部署，成為周軍拔壽陽的內應。至於此役究竟打成平手還是某一方的敗局，現存記載並沒有說得很清楚；後世史家出於為將主立名的需要，往往把它寫成某一方的勝負，這一點須與史文分開看。
peopleEn: Few names attach to this war, and they are mostly the names of commanders, with the division of roles among them differing a little between sources. On the Zhou side the campaign was set in motion by Emperor Wu of Zhou, Yuwen Yong, who had taken the throne in 560, had first cut back the branches of the Yuwen clan by putting its members to the sword, and had then reorganised the fubing and promoted tuntian, which brought Northern Zhou to a position where it could stand on equal terms with Northern Qi; what he wanted was the road from Luoyang to Jingzhou opened and Chen's northern line pushed back south of the Yangtze. The records name General Wang Gui as the commander of the Zhou army, and over the following ten years he twice broke Chen's armies, being one of the principal Zhou commanders in Henan. Sui Gong Yang Jian was chancellor at the time and served in the army as an adviser; the annals of the Sui in the House of Gao record that he came to notice through accompanying the campaigns against Chen, after which he rose step by step through the struggles for power among the Yuwen and in the end took the throne as Emperor Wen of Sui. On the Chen side the supreme command belonged to Emperor Xuan, Chen Xu, who had acceded in 559 and who, through the years of the Taijian era, had purged his court, restored the registers of households and set his commanders and ministers in order, so that the Chen was in a state to hold. The Chen officers most often connected with this campaign in the records are He Ruobi, Han Qinhu, Wu Mingche, Ouyang Wei and Yuan Junzheng: He Ruobi and Han Qinhu were veterans of the Chen who would both become celebrated commanders in the Sui conquest of Chen; Wu Mingche was the officer Chen leaned on hardest for warfare on both water and land; Ouyang Wei held Jingzhou and covered the western flank of the Luoyang battlefield; and Yuan Junzheng, as Inspector of Sizhou, was directly concerned with the forward defences. What truly determined the fate of Luoyang, though, was the defection of the Chen general Sima Xiaonan, who went over to Northern Zhou some years afterwards and disclosed the deployment of the Chen army, and it was as an inside man that the Zhou were later able to take Shouchang. Whether the campaign ended in a draw or in disaster for one side is a question the surviving accounts do not answer plainly, and later historians, with an interest in the renown of their commanders, have generally given it a shape that suits the moral purposes of the dynastic histories rather than the shape of the operations themselves.
kits: 卡面上的埃及長矛，是人類最早的一批制式刺擊兵器之一：早王朝時期的埃及人把銅或青銅矛頭裝在木杆上，用它守城垣、獵象，也用它與弓、盾配合成列；埃及人守城時習慣把長矛架在城垛口向下戳刺攀城者，這正是它最著名的用法。此役的兩軍步卒所倚重的，恰恰也是同一類東西的不同版本。南北朝的中國步卒以矛為主兵，鐵矛頭安在木柲上，槊則是加長加重的一種，供騎兵使用；此外還有戟、環首刀、弓與弩。防護上，北軍有明光鎧一類的護胸與札甲，陳軍則大量使用木胎蒙皮、髹漆的盾牌與皮甲；弓箭仍是最普及的投射兵器，弩則用於守城與伏擊。攻城器械是這一役的關鍵：北軍攜帶撞車、雲梯、巢車，並試圖掘地道與以火攻燒門樓及城上草屋，陳軍則依靠城門樓、射孔與突出的城角，配以長矛與落石拒敵。洛陽一帶北朝墓葬出土的鐵矛、鐵鏃與甲片殘件，與河南、陝西一線同期的出土品一同，勾勒出這個時代兵器形制的輪廓：矛仍然是數量最多、用途最廣的一類，也是攻城與守城兩種戰役裡都不可缺的一層。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is among the earliest standardised thrusting weapons in the history of arms: the Egyptians of the Early Dynastic period fitted a copper or bronze head to a wooden shaft, used it to hold walls, to hunt elephants, and to work alongside bow and shield in the line; its most famous employment was the defence of a wall, where the spear was laid along the parapet and thrust downward at those who tried to climb. What the foot of both armies leaned on in this campaign was precisely the same sort of thing in a different version. Chinese infantry of the Northern and Southern Dynasties took the spear as its principal arm, an iron head set on a wooden shaft, the shao being a lengthened and heavier form carried by cavalry; alongside it stood the ji, the ring-pommel sabre, the bow and the crossbow. For protection the northern army had cuirasses of the mingguan type and lamellar armour, while the Chen relied heavily on wooden shields faced with hide and lacquered, and on leather armour; the bow and arrow remained the commonest missile, and the crossbow was used for the defence of walls and for ambushes. Siege equipment was the crux of this campaign: the northern army brought up battering rams, ladders and observation towers, attempted saps, and the use of fire against the gate towers and the thatched roofs on the walls, while the Chen relied on gate towers, arrow slits and the projecting corners of the walls, with spears and stones to hold the attacker off. The iron spearheads, arrowheads and fragments of armour recovered from Northern Dynasties tombs around Luoyang, together with comparable finds in Henan and Shaanxi, give an outline of the shape of weapons in this age: the spear was still by far the most numerous and the most widely used of them all, and the one layer that no battle of siege or of defence could do without.
tactics: 洛陽之役的作戰，可以分出攻與守兩條線。進攻方第一步是集結與推進：周軍自洛州以西、以南的各處據點出發，沿黃河與洛水兩條大道東進，先掃清沿途的陳軍游騎與據點，再抵達洛陽城下，屯營於洛水北岸的平坦地帶，這一片地勢開闊，利於展開攻城器械。第二步是圍城：城東、城北各設營壘，斷絕城郊的道路，圍城打援，同時封鎖出入的糧道。第三步是強攻：以撞車撞擊城門，以雲梯附城，以巢車登高窺視城內的佈置，並在夜裡掘地道、施火攻燒門樓與城上草屋。守城的陳軍採取的是典型的以逸待勞：弓弩在上，步卒持矛與刀在城垛後待命，專以長矛刺擊攀梯者；騎兵不斷出城，襲擊周軍的糧道與攻城器械，迫其分兵；水軍利用洛水與穀水的水路，運送糧秣與援兵。兩軍相持之下，比拼的是三樣東西：攻城器械的數量與損耗、糧道的安全，還有季節。北軍拖到歲暮，北方冬令嚴寒，士卒多病，而自關中運來的糧秣既要供軍又要養驢馬，缺口越拉越大，終於在沒有決出勝負的情況下分批撤兵。南陳這邊守住了洛陽，也守住了淮南前出的據點，兩國的邊界線原封不動。
tacticsEn: The operations of the battle of Luoyang can be separated into a line of attack and a line of defence. The first stage on the attacking side was concentration and advance: the Zhou army set out from the various bases west and south of Luozhou, moving east along the two great roads of the Yellow River and the Luo, clearing the way through the Chen outposts and wandering bands on the route, and then came up to the walls of Luoyang and encamped on the open ground on the north bank of the Luo, where the terrain is flat and favourable for deploying siege equipment. The second stage was the investment: encampments were established east and north of the city, the roads around the suburbs were cut, the city was invested and relief was looked for, while the roads by which grain could enter or leave were sealed. The third stage was the assault: battering rams were brought against the gates, ladders were set against the walls, observation towers were raised to look down into the city and read its dispositions, and by night saps were driven and fire was set against the gate towers and the thatched roofs upon the walls. The Chen defence followed the classic pattern of meeting the enemy's urgency with one's own ease: bows and crossbows on the parapets above, foot soldiers with spears and sabres waiting behind the crenellations, their business being the thrusting of those who came up the ladders; cavalry rode out continually to strike at the Zhou supply line and at the siege engines, forcing the besiegers to detach; and the river craft used the waterways of the Luo and the Gu to bring up grain and reinforcements. What the two sides were really measuring against each other was three things: the number and the wear of the siege engines, the security of the supply line, and the season. The northern army held on into the depths of winter, when the cold of the north was severe and the men fell sick, and the grain coming down from Guanzhong had to feed both the soldiers and the draught animals, so that the shortfall widened; in the end, with nothing decided, they withdrew in detachments. On the Chen side Luoyang was held, and so were the forward positions in Huainan, and the line between the two states stood exactly where it had stood before.
data: 可以核對的數字不多，這場戰役的記載本身就稀疏。首先是年代：北周建德四年、南陳太建六年，即公元564年，該年為甲申年；戰役一般繫於十月開打、歲末收兵，具體月份各家說法不一。戰場是洛陽，這座城自東漢末至北魏歷代相承，考古測算的漢魏洛陽城城郭周長在二十公里上下，另有外郭與陽城，合計範圍更大；城內有宮殿官署與大倉，是北周在東部的軍資樞紐，關中運來的糧秣要在此屯放再分發。關於北軍出戰人數，文獻有從數萬到二十萬的種種說法，彼此相差十倍，這本身就說明沒有一個可核實的數字；較穩妥的估計是實際作戰兵力在數萬量級，其中騎兵與帳下兵只佔一部分，主力是步卒與隨軍的攻城工匠。圍城歷時，一般認為自十月出師到歲末北撤，前後約兩三個月，跨過嚴冬的開頭。至於交戰的損失，現存史料沒有可以核實的數目，不宜硬填；能確定的只是洛陽城沒有被攻破，陳的淮南據點在此後兩年仍然完整，這一點可由兩國後續的疆界變化反推。北周在陳的內部策反成功、拔除壽陽，是建德八年，即566年；吳明徹於彭城被俘、陳失淮南，是大建十二年，即570年；周武帝最後一次大舉伐陳兵出芒山，是578年；隋滅陳是589年。從564年排到589年，這條戰線二十五年之間的走向，都可以在這幾個年份上排出次序。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, because the record of this battle is thin to begin with. First the date: Northern Zhou's fourth year of Jiande and Chen's sixth year of Taijian, that is, 564 CE, a year that was a jiashen in the sexagenary cycle; the campaign is generally tied to the opening of the tenth month and to the withdrawal in the last months of the year, the exact months differing between sources. The battlefield was Luoyang, a city carried forward in succession from the late Eastern Han through Northern Wei; the circumference of the walls of the Han and Wei city of Luoyang, as measured archaeologically, is on the order of twenty kilometres, with the outer enclosure and the Yang city additional, so that the whole occupied area was larger still. Inside the city were the palace, the offices of the central government and the great granaries, which made it the military supply pivot of the eastern half of Northern Zhou, where the grain brought down from Guanzhong was stored and then distributed. As for the size of the northern army, the documents give figures ranging from a few tens of thousands to two hundred thousand, differing by a factor of ten, which in itself shows that no verifiable figure exists; the more defensible estimate is a field strength in the tens of thousands, of which cavalry and the men of the personal guard formed only a part, the body being infantry and the engineers and artisans who came with them for the siege. As for the length of the investment, it is generally held that from the army's departure in the tenth month to its northward withdrawal at the year's end some two or three months passed, spanning the opening of the hard winter. As for the losses of the engagement, the surviving sources give no figure that can be checked, and none should be invented; what can be established is simply that the city of Luoyang was not taken, and that Chen's forward positions in Huainan were still intact two years later, a point that can be inferred from the subsequent changes in the frontier between the two states. The Zhou penetration by which Sima Xiaonan turned over to them, and the taking of Shouchang, belong to the eighth year of Jiande, 566; Wu Mingche's capture at Pengcheng and the loss of Huainan belong to the twelfth year of Taijian, 570; Zhou Wudi's last great expedition against Chen, which went out to the Mangshan, belongs to 578; and the Sui destruction of Chen belongs to 589. Running from 564 to 589, the course of this front line over those twenty-five years can be laid out on the strength of those few years alone.
cause: 打起來的原因，遠在洛陽城下那幾十天之前。直接的原因是北周想要打破自西魏以來就存在的僵局。洛陽是北周伸向河南的尖端，正面抵住陳在淮水一線的前出據點：壽春、合肥，加上汝南一帶的城鎮，像一排楔子插在周的洛州與徐州之間。只要陳手裡還握著淮南，周的河南大平原就始終暴露在對方騎兵與步兵的威脅之下；反過來，周若能拿下洛陽以南的彭城、壽春，就等於把陳的北線推回長江，陳在江南的人力財力便可專心防守。背景的原因是雙方的國力經過了十年整頓。建德年間，周武帝宇文邕誅宗室、整軍經、重屯田，把北周推到可以持續用兵的狀態；太建年間，陳宣帝清理門戶、恢復戶口、整頓將吏，陳也處於能撐住的局面。於是衝突的節奏被戰爭本身的邏輯推著走：陳的邊軍不斷北上騷擾淮南與河南，消耗周的屯田與城防；周的軍隊不斷南下，企圖切斷陳的江陵與淮南之間的水陸聯運。還有一層是外交上的虛實。兩國在邊境上有使節往來，有榷場互市，桌面上是兄弟之國的說法，桌下卻是年年開打。建德三年，也就是563年，周軍第一次南下便無功而返；兩年之後的這一次，是在同一條戰線上的第二次嘗試，而陳宣帝此時已經明白，關鍵的戰場不在野外，而在城下。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting lay well before the few dozen days under the walls of Luoyang. The immediate reason was that Northern Zhou wanted to break the deadlock that had existed since Western Wei. Luoyang was the point Northern Zhou thrust out into Henan, and it faced squarely the forward Chen bases along the Huai: Shouchun, Hefei, and the towns around Runan, a row of wedges driven between Zhou's Luozhou and Xuzhou. As long as Chen still held Huainan, the great plain of Henan on the Zhou side lay permanently exposed to the enemy's cavalry and infantry; conversely, if Zhou could take Pengcheng and Shouchang south of Luoyang, it would push Chen's northern line back to the Yangtze, and the Chen's man and wealth in the south could be set entirely to defence. Behind this lay the fact that both states had spent ten years putting their strength in order. In the years of Jiande, Zhou Wudi Yuwen Yong put the clan to the sword, reformed the military administration and made heavy of tuntian, bringing Northern Zhou to a condition in which it could wage war continuously; in the years of Taijian, Chen Xuan cleared his court, restored the registers of households and set his commanders and ministers in order, so that the Chen was in a condition to endure. From then on the rhythm of the conflict was carried along by the logic of the war itself: Chen's frontier troops rode north again and again to harry Huainan and Henan, wearing down Zhou's fields and garrisons; Zhou's armies marched south again and again, seeking to cut the water and land link between Chen's Jiangling and its Huainan. There was a further layer in the contrast between diplomatic appearance and reality. Between the two states envoys went back and forth and markets were held along the frontier; on the surface they were brother states, and beneath the table they fought every year. In the third year of Jiande, that is 563, a Zhou army had gone south and returned without result; the campaign of two years later was a second attempt along the same front, and by that time Emperor Xuan of Chen had grasped that the decisive ground was not in the open country but beneath the walls.
impact: 洛陽之役的直接後果，是北周的第二次南征又告落空，而南陳安然度過了一次北伐。短期看，這一役延續了邊界的均勢：陳的壽春、合肥等前出據點一座未失，周的洛州守住了河南的門戶，兩國的實際接觸線仍舊停在淮水一線，誰也沒有把對方推回去。真正深遠的影響有兩條。第一條是北周內部的權力轉移。此役之後，宇文邕對外用兵頻仍而對內防範更嚴，楊堅在軍中經歷了伐陳的實戰考驗，地位更加穩固；及至578年周武帝在芒山陣亡、579年宇文護被誅，北周迅即崩解，隋室代周的種子，正是在這十餘年裡一場場邊境戰役中埋下的。第二條是戰略的轉向。洛陽城下攻不克的經驗，逼得北周改變打法：既然正面攻城無效，便轉而倚重內應與側翼的奇襲。建德八年，也就是566年，陳將司馬消難以州降周，暴露了壽陽的防禦部署，周軍乘隙拔除壽陽，陳國第一次失去淮南之地，前線從此退到江淮之間。陳為此付出了更大的代價：大建十二年（570年）吳明徹在彭城被俘，淮南再失，直到589年隋滅陳，陳都再沒能收復壽陽。洛陽之役本身在史書上並不常被當作轉折點，但只要把564年、566年、570年、589年四個年份連起來看，就會發現一條清楚的線：北周在洛陽沒能打開缺口，卻在壽陽打開了缺口；陳守住了洛陽，卻沒守住淮南。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the battle of Luoyang was that the Zhou's second expedition southward came to nothing again, while the Chen rode out a Northern invasion unharmed. In the short term the battle preserved the balance on the frontier: not one of Chen's forward positions, at Shouchun or Hefei or elsewhere, was lost, and Zhou's Luozhou held the gateway of Henan, so that the line of actual contact between the two states remained on the Huai and neither side pushed the other back. Two of the deeper consequences deserve naming. The first is the internal redistribution of power in Northern Zhou. After this campaign Yuwen Yong went on campaign abroad while guarding more strictly against the clan at home, and Yang Jian had passed through the fire of a real war against Chen in the army, which made his position yet more secure; and when Zhou Wudi was killed at the Mangshan in 578 and Yuwen Hu was executed in 579, Northern Zhou collapsed in short order, and the seed of the Sui replacing the Zhou was planted precisely in these border campaigns of the dozen years that followed. The second is the turning of strategy. The lesson of failing to take Luoyang forced the Zhou to change their method: if frontal siege would not work, they would rely on insiders and on strikes at the flank. In the eighth year of Jiande, that is 566, the Chen general Sima Xiaonan handed over his prefecture to the Zhou and exposed the defences of Shouchang, and the Zhou army took Shouchang on the opening; the Chen lost Huainan for the first time and the front fell back to the region between the Yangtze and the Huai. The Chen paid a larger price still for this: in the twelfth year of Taijian, 570, Wu Mingche was captured at Pengcheng and Huainan was lost again, and the Chen never recovered Shouchang before the Sui destroyed them in 589. The battle of Luoyang is not often treated in the histories as a turning point, but if one lays the four years 564, 566, 570 and 589 side by side, a clear line appears: the Northern Zhou failed to open a breach at Luoyang and opened one at Shouchang instead, and the Chen held Luoyang and lost Huainan.
result: 打完了：洛陽城沒有被攻下，北周無功而還，南陳守住了這座北方名都與它背後的河南糧倉。結果可以分三層來說。第一層是戰役本身。圍城的北軍用盡了撞車、雲梯與掘地道的手段，卻沒能在城門上打開缺口；守城的陳軍以弓弩壓制梯隊、以長矛刺擊攀城者、以騎兵切斷糧道，雙方在洛水兩岸相持到歲末，北軍因糧秣不繼與天氣寒冷而分批北撤，陳軍也沒有能力趁勢反攻河南。第二層是洛陽的價值。這座城自東漢末到北魏是歷代王朝的東都，城郭宮苑之完整、倉儲之富庶，在當時的中原無出其右；正因如此，它在北周與隋的手裡一直是北方經營南方的兵站與糧站，589年隋滅陳時，楊堅正是以洛陽為總部調度賀若弼、韓擒虎等路兵馬順流東下。第三層是這一役在南北朝末局裡的位置。它證明陳的江防與淮南兩道屏障仍然有效，也證明北周要吞併陳，光靠河南的城池頂不住；此後北方的努力轉向內部的整合、屯田與制度，二十年後由隋在洛陽完成。對陳來說，這一役的結果是代價最小的拖延：它買到了三到五年的時間，也買到了隋軍打到建康時國內早已凋敝、上下離心這個隱患的機會。
resultEn: It was over: the city of Luoyang was not taken, the Northern Zhou returned without result, and the Chen held this famous northern city and the Henan granary behind it. The outcome can be set out in three layers. The first is the battle itself. The besieging northern army exhausted its means of battering rams, ladders and saps without opening a breach in the gates; the Chen on the walls kept down the ladders with bow and crossbow, thrust at those who came up them with the spear, and cut the supply line with cavalry, and the two sides stood facing each other along the Luo until the end of the year, when the northern army, short of grain and pressed by the cold, withdrew in detachments, while the Chen had no strength to counterattack into Henan. The second is the worth of Luoyang. From the late Eastern Han to Northern Wei this city was the eastern capital of one dynasty after another, and neither the completeness of its walls and palace nor the richness of its granaries had any equal in the Central Plain of the time; precisely for that reason it remained, in the hands of Northern Zhou and then of the Sui, the mustering and supply base from which the north organised the south, and when the Sui destroyed the Chen in 589 it was from Luoyang as headquarters that Yang Jian directed the columns of He Ruobi, Han Qinhu and the rest down the river. The third is the place of this battle in the endgame of the Northern and Southern Dynasties. It showed that the Chen's river defence and the two barriers of Huainan still held, and it showed that Northern Zhou could not swallow the Chen relying on the cities of Henan alone; the effort of the north afterwards turned inward, to integration, to tuntian and to institutions, and was completed by the Sui at Luoyang twenty years later. For the Chen the result of this campaign was a postponement bought at the smallest price: it bought three to five years, and it bought the opportunity that would present itself when the Sui armies reached Jiankang to find a country already exhausted and its rulers and commanded estranged from one another.
